baseline.scope: source-state VM; no browser or paint timing
limitations: Visibility and DOM are boundary doubles; the native loop and prayer-selection/publication functions are source-bound.
All five pre-hide and return expectations are independently specified for each synthetic UTC scenario.
Repeats are deterministic fixture repetitions, not independent hardware/browser trials.
configSha256 binds the config text executed by the VM, including any SALAH_REQUEST_CONFIG override.
A callback is not a presented frame; no screenshot, bfcache, real tab return, dispatch duration or human judgment is claimed.
The whole-render positive control is test-only and is not an approved production correction.

prayer.scope: actual prayer publisher and loop in VM; optional rendering, DOM layout and transport are boundary doubles
limitations: Not a native first-frame or dispatch-cost measurement.
The restoring task still performs the existing synchronous Moon request after prayer; this does not eliminate its task cost.
Helper extraction is an experimental source transformation, not an accepted production change.

misses.reason: preview final publication lacks currentness headroom

preview.scope: real preview owner and solar-mask publication; numerical renderer, canvas, layout, detail and clock doubles
limitations: A single full upload removes this two-write failure window only; atomic browser/GPU upload is not proved.
Moon detail composition precedes final background publication and can have its own side effects; no cross-owner transaction is claimed.
Expired weather changes accepted authority even when its physical inputs later renew identically. No relaxed currentness or held-weather rule is implemented.

crossOwner.scope: Actual Moon detail adoption, projection, join, encoding and canvas publication run inside the actual preview and solar-mask publication path. Atmospheric fields, canvas storage, layout, native host and decode transport are controlled fixtures. Buffer ordering does not establish a painted frame.

retention.scope: actual runtime scope/clock/phase predicates; hypothetical quarantined metadata, no receiver composition
limitations: This evaluates re-admission constraints; it does not implement storage, byte custody, disposal or a public reuse path.
Reuse also needs valid physical/profile identity and receiver bytes at the new adoption boundary; this predicate experiment alone is insufficient.
No current pixels are kept during hide, no elapsed-time grace period is introduced, and no performance saving is measured.
